text: dsh-workspace-browser 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的工作区浏览插件，通过 Cordis 客户端槽位替换侧栏工作区区域，并在对话首页提供工作区选择器。它提供最近会话与可折叠分区、项目编辑器和会话行操作，可固定、重命名、分叉或归档会话；也可为工作区添加多个源文件夹、设置主目录，并在提示上下文中列出附加目录。适合需要整理项目工作区、管理会话或让会话了解多个源码目录的 DSH 用户。代码未声明 API Key 或外部服务依赖。

dsh-workspace-browser adds Recents, collapsible sections, project editing, and session actions to DSH Web. Users can pin, rename, fork, or archive sessions, switch workspaces from the conversation picker, and add source folders listed in prompt context. No API key or external service is declared.
想在 DSH 侧栏查看最近会话并整理不同工作区。
我想给一个项目工作区添加多个源码目录，让会话知道这些文件夹。
How can I pin, rename, fork, or archive conversations from the workspace sidebar?
dsh-workspace-browser 的侧栏功能：在 DSH 工作区侧栏查看最近会话与可折叠分区，并通过项目编辑器管理工作区；会话行菜单可固定、重命名、分叉或归档会话。
dsh-workspace-browser 的多目录项目功能：在项目编辑器为工作区添加源文件夹并选择主目录；插件持久化目录列表，并把附加路径写入相关会话的提示上下文。

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · dsh-workspace-browser：Standalone Cordis client plugin that gives the shipped dsh web client the workspace features it does not have: the sidebar **Recents** section, collapsible section headers, the **project editor** with extra source folders, pin/rename/fork/archive row actions, search, shortcuts, and the conversation-hero **workspace picker**. In the project editor a folder's own name opens that folder in the OS file manager, and a conversation whose own folder has vanished is silently re-rooted to the Workspace's primary folder when it is opened.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Why it exists：The 2026-09-29 Desktop build (**0.2.0-rc.2**) shipped a workspace browser with no Recents, no collapsible sections and no project editor. By **0.2.1-rc.2** the in-tree `ui-workspace` is that browser (toast factory, inline session-id copy, shared hover dwell, session watermarks, remote-access hooks) but still has no Recents section, no project editor and no folder API. This plugin still replaces that row: the rc.2 contracts come from the in-tree snapshot, and the plugin layer on top is Recents, the project editor, and the plugin-owned source-folder list.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Why it exists：`cordis.patch.yml` disables the in-tree `ui-workspace` row and inserts this package as `ui-workspace-browser`. A `name` override cannot do that swap: the include loader treats `name` as an identity check and skips the patch when it does not match, so the stock browser would keep running and this plugin's Recents, project editor, and source folders would never mount. Both claim the same slots, locale namespace (`workspace`) and `ctx.uiWorkspace` service, so only one may be enabled. While this bundle is selected, `ui-workspace-browser` must stay enabled — disabling only that row leaves nobody providing the service and web boot times out. A bundle whose slots never register therefore leaves the workspace region **empty**, which is why the client-half surface is checked against the host before any install (see Verification).

text: @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Source folders on a host without the folder API：That sentence is the whole mechanism: the host's `workspace-write` policy still resolves a single root (`session.header.cwd`), so the plugin can widen what the model *knows*, never what it may *write*. Under `danger-full-access` the write caveat is moot. Nothing is injected when the Workspace has no extra folder, when the Session is unknown to the registry, or when the host has no `systemPrompt` service.

text: @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Source folders on a host without the folder API：*Set as primary* asks the node half to move the host record itself. The host exposes no remote repath API to call, so the node half drives the workspace registry's own write path in process (`POST /api/workspace-browser/primary`, [src/index.ts](src/index.ts)): it canonicalizes the directory with `realpath`, refuses a path that is missing, is not a directory, or that another Workspace already owns, and rewrites the record's `path` through `mutate`, so the host itself later treats the promoted folder as the Workspace path. The viewing store still records the promotion and keeps the previous directory as an extra folder, which is the fallback for a host that cannot be repathed; a refusal only warns, so the editor still switches. Later New Session creates with that `cwd` alone (the shipped host accepts a create that sends `cwd` and no `workspaceId`), and the browser borrows the Session back by `cwd`. @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Install：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:lihongxu0221/dsh-workspace-browser
```

The GUI plugin manager does the same. `cordis.patch.yml` is declared by `dsh.bundle.patch`, so it must stay in `files`: a packed package (git or npm install) that lacks it is rejected with `failed to read overlay`.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Install：The host composes plugin node halves at startup, so a change to `lib/index.js` shows up only after the app restarts — including the prompt context below, whose text is resolved at every Session prompt assembly. The client half is unaffected by that restart rule.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Build：```powershell
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck              # against the generation pinned in devDependencies
pnpm run build                  # tsc: src -> lib/types, then scripts/bundle-node.mjs -> lib/index.js
node scripts/build-client.mjs   # harness client preset: lib/types -> lib/client.js (+ lib/index.js)

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Build：`scripts/bundle-node.mjs` is the fallback for the node half when no harness checkout is available: it concatenates `lib/types` into the single-file `lib/index.js` the package entry names, which is exactly the transformation the preset's Node build face performs for these three modules. The client half still needs the preset.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Build：`scripts/build-client.mjs` uses the client-bundle preset from a dsh source checkout (`packages/client/tsdown.client.ts`, default `..\..\deepseek-harness`, override with `$DSH_HARNESS` or an argument). The preset resolves a package through `packages/<group>/<dir>/package.json`, so the script stages a temporary face package inside the checkout, links this repo's `node_modules` into it, runs tsdown for the Client face, normalizes the checkout path out of the emitted banners, copies the artifacts back and deletes the staging directory. The checkout itself is left untouched.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Verification：1. **Types.** `devDependencies` pins every `@deepseek-ai/*` package to the published generation this plugin targets (`0.2.1-rc.2`; cordis `^4.0.5`), so `pnpm run typecheck` fails on any atom, prop or service that generation lacks. The three host folder APIs are still absent from the published surface and are declared optional locally — the project editor falls back to the plugin's own store when they are missing. The client inject list also names `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-remote-access`, which the rc.2 `remoteAccess` service comes from.
2. **Bundle surface.** Diff the bundle against the host build: extract the host's own `dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace/lib/client.js` from `resources/app.asar`, then compare the `//#region lib/types/...` module lists and the member sets required from each module-table entry (`_deepseek_ai_dsh_client_ui_primitives.X`, `…dsh_client_store.X`, `_deepseek_ai_dsh_cordis.X`, `react.X`, `react_jsx_runtime.X`), and check every required primitives symbol against the host's single `export { … }` list. @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace-browser README · Known gaps：- **A repath the host refuses leaves the registry path alone.** The shipped host publishes no remote repath API, so the node half moves the record through the registry's own write path. A host with no `workspaceRegistry` service — or one whose registry exposes neither `get` nor a movable entity — is refused with a message, and the viewing-store layer stays the fallback: the plugin remembers the promoted directory, starts new Sessions there while it still exists, and borrows them back by cwd. The browser warns instead of failing, and the editor still switches.
- **A Session whose folder was deleted is never restored into it.** Startup and New Session probe the directory over `GET /api/workspace-browser/directory` before reusing a blank Session or restoring the last one; a deleted `cwd` stays reachable under Recents, and the replacement Session starts at the Workspace's effective primary folder instead. When that primary folder has itself disappeared the plugin refuses the New Session with a message naming the path, so the host never recreates the deleted folder.
